metadata.note: The Massachusetts Central / Central Massachusetts Railroad: Boston - North Cambridge - Waltham - Wayland - South Sudbury - Hudson - Berlin - (Clinton) - Oakdale - Jefferson - Rutland - Barre - Ware - Belchertown - Amherst - Northampton, 104 mi. The Massachusetts Central ran its own trains 1 Oct 1881 - 16 May 1883 and failed; NO trains ran 16 May 1883 - 28 Sep 1885; the reorganized Central Massachusetts Railroad never ran a train under its own name - the Boston and Lowell ran them from the 1885 restart (lease 7 Dec 1886) and the Boston and Maine from 1 Apr 1887, as its 'Central Massachusetts Branch'. Features are split by operator (Rule 4) and wherever the drawn alignment or the end year changes: the line died from the west inward (Ware - Northampton 1917 / 1932, Clinton - Northampton 1932, Berlin - Clinton 1958, South Sudbury - Hudson 1965, Boston - South Sudbury 26 Nov 1971) and was relocated twice (Wachusett Reservoir 1903; inner end onto the Fitchburg main at Clematis Brook 1951-52). Inner-end and junction pieces ride other lines (the B&L / Lowell line and Fitchburg Division into Boston, the Worcester & Nashua Clinton - Oakdale, the Central Vermont Canal Jct - Norwottuck Jct 1931-32, the Fitchburg Marlborough Branch beyond Gleason Jct); each feature's geometry_quality says which. From 18 Jan 1965 the MBTA subsidized this service, but the B&M kept running the trains under contract to the end, so the B&M stays the operator through 1971 (report flags the repo's MBTA-era split convention as a maintainer decision). The modern 'Massachusetts Central Railroad' short line (1975-, South Barre / Ware / Palmer) is an unrelated freight company and is not drawn. Omitted per the research report's drawable: NONE: the Holden Jct - Carr Jct connector (no confirmable passenger year), Mellen's Hampden Railroad (built 1913, never opened), and the freight-only Wheelwright Branch (1939-1979).
sources: Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952, Boston and Maine suburban table list (Table 43 title only: Boston - Gleasondale - Hudson - Clinton; times not recoverable)
B&MRHS, The Central Mass (Marker Press, 2nd ed. 2008, ISBN 978-0-9662736-3-2) - cited page by page by WP-CM; not consulted directly

metadata.freight_only_audit: Built to Rule 1 from the start: no segment runs past the end of passenger service. Trimmed per the report: Clinton/Oakdale - Northampton after 23 Apr 1932 (local freight to 1938); Gleason Jct - Marlborough after 1939; Berlin - Clinton after 1958; South Sudbury - Hudson after Jan 1965 and Boston - South Sudbury after 26 Nov 1971 (freight into the late 1970s); the Wheelwright Branch (1939-79), Hampden Railroad, Fort Devens - Sudbury Annex spur, B&A Ware River freight connections and Wachusett construction trackage are not drawn.

not_yet_sourced: Ware - Northampton 1917 - 1928: WP-CM says passenger service was discontinued Aug 1917 (CM p.45) but also that one through train ran Boston - Northampton 'by 1928' and that Northampton service ended 23 Apr 1932 (CM pp.48-49). No restoration date found; 1917-1928 is left undrawn and the 1928-1932 span (incl. the 1931-32 Central Vermont trackage) depends on the second reading. A 1918-1927 B&M timetable would settle it.
Gleason Jct - Marlborough: START [OPEN] - 1902 is the year the connection was built, not a dated first passenger train.
Gleason Jct - Hudson (FIT): start bracket 1950-1951 (CM Hudson closed 30 Dec 1950); drawn from 1951.
Oakdale - Jefferson: Jefferson opening conflict, narrative 19 Dec 1881 vs station table June 1882; drawn from 1882 for the Massachusetts Central.
Jefferson - Ware: whether passengers ran before the 19 Dec 1887 through opening (Ware station 27 Jun 1887).
Exact date passenger service ended west of Berlin in early 1958.
Clinton terminal routing 1903-1958 (East Switch wye vs Clinton Jct) and how 1951-58 Clinton trains served Hudson (FIT).
Inner-end route into Boston 1927-1952 (after North Cambridge station closed 24 Apr 1927).
Poughkeepsie Bridge Route through trains (Philadelphia & Washington Express, Harrisburg Express): years and extent over the CM.
Every headway_min and avg_speed_kmh is an estimate; the only sourced figures are the train counts quoted in the segment notes.
MBTA 1965-1971: B&M kept as operator (it ran the trains); the repo's MBTA-era split convention is a maintainer decision.

segments.note: Massachusetts Central Railroad's own operation: grand opening Boston - Hudson 1 Oct 1881 (first schedule 4 round trips Boston - Hudson plus 4 Boston - Waltham), first through train from Jefferson 19 Dec 1881; the company bought five locomotives and ran its own trains until it failed and suspended all service on 16 May 1883 (WP-CM citing B&MRHS 'The Central Mass' pp.7-10). The 1880 B&L lease never took effect. No trains at all ran 16 May 1883 - 28 Sep 1885, so nothing is drawn for 1884. Drawn Boston - Waltham - Hudson - Berlin and over the ORIGINAL pre-reservoir line South Clinton - Boylston - West Boylston to Oakdale (the 1903 relocation did not yet exist). Headway is an estimate from the 4 Boston - Hudson round trips (Waltham locals more frequent inside Waltham, through trains beyond Hudson fewer).
sources: Segment-level: start 1 Oct 1881 / 19 Dec 1881 and end 16 May 1883 from WP-CM (History; station table) citing B&MRHS, The Central Mass, pp.7-10; Fowler confirms 1890s service at every station, not these dates. (research/branches/central_massachusetts_railroad.txt compiled these from the cited pages; the tracer did not re-read the source text)

segments.note: Boston and Lowell era: service restarted 28 Sep 1885, the B&L running the trains by contract for the new Central Massachusetts Railroad (formal lease 7 Dec 1886); resumed schedule 7 round trips Boston - Jefferson and 10 Boston - Waltham, Jefferson service from 14 Dec 1885. Ends 31 Mar 1887 when the B&M leased the B&L (WP-CM). Split at the 1885 restart, not the 1886 lease, because the B&L ran the trains from the first day (Rule 4). Drawn over the original pre-reservoir alignment Berlin - South Clinton - West Boylston - Oakdale. Headway is an estimate from the 7 Jefferson + 10 Waltham round trips (the Waltham locals make the inner end busier than this; the Jefferson end sees less).

segments.note: The B&M ran these trains from its lease of the B&L, 1 Apr 1887 (it bought the CM corporation outright 20 Feb 1902 - a corporate tidy-up, not an operator change; New Haven stock control 1907-13 likewise). Inner end into Boston over the B&L main line and the CM's own North Cambridge Jct - Hill Crossing - Clematis Brook double track, which the CM kept parallel to the Fitchburg Division until 1951-52, when the B&M joined the two at Clematis Brook and closed the CM's Belmont and Waverley stations. Ends 1952 for that reason (an alignment change, not an end of service - see the post-1952 feature). Report UNRESOLVED 10: whether the approach changed earlier, when North Cambridge station closed 24 Apr 1927, is not established. Headway is an estimate: 1887 schedule 3 Boston - Northampton + 2 Boston - Hudson + 3 Boston - Wayland plus Waltham locals; four round trips by 1950 (WP-SS).

properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror), traced with opstrace.py on 0.25-degree rail sub-tiles plus every way tagged old_railway_operator ~ B&M / Boston & Maine / Central Mass / Massachusetts Central and rail-trail / abandoned ways fetched over each lifted stretch; ways NAMED for the Mass Central Rail Trail / Norwottuck Rail Trail counted as own track even where OSM mis-tags them old_railway_operator=NYNH&H; the 'Unused Central Massachusetts Railroad Grade' (1870s grading) was excluded. Where the router would not follow a fragmented grade, OSM ways were chained by id in order. OpenHistoricalMap was queried for every lifted stretch (inner Cambridge/Belmont, Waltham - Hudson, the Wachusett Reservoir, Oakdale - Ware, Ware - Northampton) and returned nothing. Junction and station points were read off OSM ways (e.g. Clematis Brook, Gleason Jct, West Berlin Jct, East Switch, Clinton Jct, Canal Jct, Norwottuck Jct); Nominatim geocodes were used only as rough waypoints and several were discarded as wrong (South Clinton -> a river, Wayside Inn -> a brook, Belmont Center -> a car-repair shop, Oakdale -> a cemetery).
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 5.2 mi in all against documented ~4.8 mi Gleason Jct - Marlborough (OG52 table title: Gleasondale 25.4, Hudson 27.7, Marlboro 31.1 from Boston; WP-CM Gleason Jct 26.28). No straight-line legs. [5.2 mi] Gleason Jct - C.M. Jct - Hudson (Fitchburg station) - Marlborough on OSM ways of the Assabet River Rail Trail, chained in order, no straight legs. This is the Fitchburg Railroad's Marlborough Branch (B&M after 1900), not CM property; the 1902 Gleason Jct - C.M. Jct connector is not separately mapped and is drawn where the trail meets the CM. ERA CAVEAT: drawn on the grades as OSM maps them at or after abandonment; station-area track layouts of earlier decades are not reconstructed.

segments.note: Boston - Gleasondale - Hudson - Marlborough trains turning off the CM at Gleason Jct onto the Fitchburg Railroad's Marlborough Branch (B&M lessee from 1900) via the connection the B&M built after its 1902 purchase of the CM 'to enable passenger service into Marlborough'. START IS [OPEN]: 1902 is the year the connection was built (Gleason Junction 'opened 1902'); no source dates the first passenger train over it, so 1902 is the earliest possible year, not a confirmed one. Ends 1939 ('In 1939 the B&M ended passenger service to Marlborough'); OG52's Sept 1951 'Marlboro 31.1 miles, freight service only' is consistent and is NOT a passenger end. Headway is an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: 1902 connection and 1939 end from WP-CM (B&M section; Decline in the east; station table rows Gleason Jct, Hudson (FIT), Marlborough) and WP-SS; the first passenger year is unsourced. [1.5 mi] Gleason Jct - C.M. Jct - Hudson (Fitchburg station) on the east section of the Assabet River Rail Trail (Marlborough Branch grade), chained, no straight legs. Rides the Marlborough Branch, not CM track; the Hudson (FIT) platform point is the trail's bend at Hudson, not separately located. ERA CAVEAT: drawn on the grades as OSM maps them at or after abandonment; station-area track layouts of earlier decades are not reconstructed.

segments.note: After the CM Hudson station closed 30 Dec 1950, Hudson passengers used the Fitchburg Railroad's Hudson station on the Marlborough Branch, reached from Gleason Jct ('Passenger traffic moved to Hudson Station on the Marlborough Branch until January 17, 1965'). Start bracket 1950-1951; 1951 is the first full year, drawn as the confirmed start. 1958-1965 the line's last trains beyond South Sudbury ended here: two weekday trains in 1958, one round trip from 14 Jun 1959; last 17 Jan 1965 (MBTA's first act on the line was the 18 Jan cutback). How the 1951-58 Clinton trains served this station is not established (report UNRESOLVED 8). Headway is an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: 30 Dec 1950 move and 17 Jan 1965 end from WP-CM (Decline in the east; station table). (research/branches/central_massachusetts_railroad.txt compiled these from the cited pages; the tracer did not re-read the source text)
